result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the fear of scarcity—the deep-seated belief that there isn’t enough to go around. This fear fuels greed, hoarding, violence, and systemic oppression, all of which distort human potential and divide us.

Imagine a world where resources (food, knowledge, love, time) are shared freely, not hoarded or weaponized. Where competition is replaced by collaboration, and success is measured by collective well-being rather than individual accumulation. Where education and empathy are prioritized over control, and where no one has to justify their existence or worth.

This isn’t about utopia—it’s about dismantling the illusion that scarcity is inevitable. If we could shift our collective mindset from "not enough" to "enough for all," the ripple effects would transform everything: economies, governments, relationships, even our relationship with the planet.

What would *you* change if fear of scarcity didn’t exist?
